summary: Add a visual link between the circle properties and coordinate methods, then deepen multi-step practice beyond the existing direct questions.

improvements.why: The note states the chord and tangent properties but has no figure showing the midpoint, perpendicular, and point of contact together.
improvements.what: Use a graph_sketch with a sampled circular outline, labelled centre and contact point, a horizontal chord with its midpoint marked, the perpendicular from the centre to that midpoint, and a tangent perpendicular to a labelled radius. Keep the coordinate positions and labels consistent; explain in the note what the learner should notice.

improvements.why: The ten existing items include only one multi-step tangent equation and no question requiring a complete circle equation from diameter endpoints.
improvements.what: Add one exam-style structured item using non-horizontal diameter endpoints: calculate the midpoint centre, half-length radius, and circle equation, showing each step. Add one contrasting MCQ with a midpoint/radius-squared misconception distractor.

improvements.why: The chord property is tested only by finding the midpoint of a horizontal chord; the angle-in-a-semicircle property is tested mainly by recall.
improvements.what: Add an exam-style chord problem with an oblique chord requiring midpoint and perpendicular gradient to find an unknown centre coordinate; add a Show that or Prove item using a diameter and a verified third point on the circle to establish perpendicular lines, with full working and a geometrical reason.

improvements.where: pack worked and note, after the existing worked example
improvements.why: The single worked example teaches tangent gradients, leaving the chord and diameter properties without a modelled coordinate solution.
improvements.what: Add one worked example with a faded version that uses a chord midpoint and its perpendicular bisector to locate a circle centre, then obtains the radius and equation. In the note, add a concise matching worked calculation and a self-test asking the learner to justify the midpoint step.
